content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — reduce initial forecast peaks.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — adjust downward bias by +0.5–1.0% relative to recent mean.
- Overshoot after sharp sentiment spikes — cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2.0% above recent 7-day high.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 30-day mean, reduce by 0.3–0.5σ per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment rises >0.8 over 3–5 days, forecast should adjust upward by 0.1–0.3 points per day, not just react to current value.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — smooth sentiment transitions with 3-day moving average before weighting into forecast.
